audit.whatIsWrong: The single worst error in this matchup: the page states 'Galio's passive Winds of War reveals stealthed units and shreds magic damage sustain, directly countering your Twilight Shroud playstyle.' Every clause is false. Winds of War is his Q, not his passive. His passive is Colossal Smash — a periodic empowered auto dealing bonus magic damage in an area. And NOTHING in Galio's kit reveals stealth, so the shroud works normally against him. The same fiction is repeated in whys[0], spikes[0].text, mid and wants.you[1], and it tells a paying Akali player not to use her defining ability.
audit.why: Riot's own text: P 'Every few seconds, Galio's next basic attack deals bonus magic damage in an area'; Q 'Galio fires two windblasts that converge into a large tornado that deals damage over time'. No reveal, no magic-sustain shred. Also corrected: Shield of Durand does not 'punish any dash-in' — it is a charge Galio holds while moving slowly, at 275 range, so walking away beats it. And its release taunts everyone NEARBY, an area effect, so the shroud hides you from his aim but not from the zone.
audit.corrected: early, mid, spikes[0].text, whys[0], whys[2], wants.you[1], dontsFull[0].d and dontsFull[1].d rewritten around Colossal Smash, Winds of War as an 825-range Q, and Shield of Durand as a 275-range charge.

audit.whatIsWrong: Rows 2 through 6 disagreed between layers: phases[].side read Skill on all five while win[] read Galio on all seven. The full-layer ratings also gave Galio-owned rows 6/10 in Akali's favour, which reads backwards.
audit.why: 47.76% over 1292 games means Galio is genuinely ahead, but not on every single row — Akali has real windows at level 3 once the shroud lands and at first item inside the Justice Punch cooldown gap.
audit.corrected: Reconciled chart, both layers, matched pairs: Galio, Galio, Skill, Galio, Galio, Skill, Galio, with ratings corrected to sit below 5/10 on Galio rows.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 was described as 'flash-taunt into your backline from across the map' — Hero's Entrance does not taunt. It shields allies in the landing area and knocks up nearby enemies on arrival.
audit.why: Riot's R text. Range 4000/4750/5500, cooldown 180/160/140 — the long cooldown is the real planning number and it was absent.
audit.corrected: phases[4].why, whys[4] and breakdown.cooldowns rewritten around the shield, the knockup and the 180-second rank-1 cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'take the fifteen-second invitation' — a fabricated number.
audit.why: Justice Punch is 11/10/9/8/7. Shield of Durand is 18/17/16/15/14. Winds of War is 11/10/9/8/7. Hero's Entrance is 180/160/140.
audit.corrected: Real numbers written into breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, dosFull[2].d, breakdown.feeding and several whys.

edits.before: Galio's passive Winds of War reveals stealthed units and shreds magic damage sustain, directly countering your Twilight Shroud playstyle. His Shield of Durand punishes any dash-in attempt with a taunt that locks you in place for his allies or jungler to follow up. Play very passive, farm with Q from range, and avoid all-in attempts since he trades evenly or better even without landing much.
edits.after: Galio's passive is Colossal Smash — every few seconds his next auto deals bonus damage in an area, and that wind-up is your cue to step back. Winds of War is his Q, an 825-range tornado that out-ranges your 550 Q. Shield of Durand is a charge he holds while moving slowly, at only 275 range, so the taunt is beaten by walking away rather than by dashing in. Farm with Q from range and avoid all-ins.

edits.before: Level 6 is where the matchup gets dangerous for you: Hero's Entrance lets him flash across the map and taunt-lock a teammate, meaning he doesn't even need to win lane to win the game. In lane, his passive continues to counter your stealth engage, so look to roam yourself rather than force anything in a losing lane. Ban or dodge consideration aside, prioritize wave management and vision over trades.
edits.after: Level 6 is where the matchup gets dangerous: Hero's Entrance shields his whole team and knocks up on landing from up to 5500 range, so he wins other lanes without ever beating you in yours. Nothing in his kit reveals stealth, so the shroud still works — but Shield of Durand's release taunts everyone nearby, so hide from his aim, not from the zone. Track his 180-second R and roam yourself.
